claims.text: The proposed material is a nanoscale multilayer coating containing FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The initial multilayer has a predominantly random elemental distribution together with local chemical clustering.
Severe lattice distortion is responsible for the initial local chemical clustering or latent SRO.
Randomly distributed elements with different atomic radii produce severe lattice distortion in HEAs.
Sustained mechanical loading drives a transition in local SRO at FCC/BCC multilayer interfaces.
The loading-induced transition changes the interfaces from a relatively disordered, clustered state to a more ordered state.
High-strain deformation can promote atomistic rearrangements in an HEA.
Under sustained loading, stress localizes at the nanoscale layer interfaces.
Interfacial stress localization promotes atomic rearrangements that increase SRO.
Increasing interfacial order changes the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation and motion.
The resulting change in dislocation mobility progressively accommodates plastic flow under creep conditions.
Stress-induced interfacial SRO evolution governs progressive plastic deformation in nanoscale FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
This pathway differs from deformation in conventional metallic multilayers because HEAs have greater compositional complexity and lattice distortion.
Loaded samples will develop more interfacial SRO than the as-deposited baseline.
The increase in SRO will correlate with changes in dislocation density and mobility.
Loaded samples will exhibit a progressive shift in stress-strain behavior consistent with a changed deformation mechanism.
The mechanism should dominate when nanoscale layer dimensions make interface effects pronounced.
The mechanism may not apply to substantially thicker layers or to bulk HEAs without defined interfaces.
Otherwise identical samples with deliberately modified or disrupted interfacial SRO provide the proposed controlled comparison.
Failure to observe a reproducible interfacial SRO increase, or failure of deformation to correlate with SRO evolution, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
